chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him: 'I have felt compassionate concern about the curse of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) against Yaqteen and what he fathered.'

So he said: 'O Abu al-Hasan! It is not as you suppose. The believer in the loins of a disbeliever is like a pebble in a mud brick. The rain comes and washes away the mud brick, but does not harm the pebble in the slightest.'

key_terms.أَشْفَقْتُ: Felt compassionate concern, pity, or apprehension (ashfaqtu) — a nuanced term encompassing both sympathy and anxious worry
key_terms.الْحَصَاة فِي اللَّبِنَة: The pebble in the mud brick — the central metaphor of the hadith expressing the believer's protection from punishment meant for disbelievers
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُ فِي صُلْبِ الْكَافِرِ: The believer in the loins of the disbeliever — a believer descended from or born to a disbeliever's lineage
key_terms.دَعْوَة: Supplication or curse (da'wa) — here referring to a curse or imprecation directed against someone
key_terms.صُلْب: The loins or back (sulb) — in classical Arabic, the origin of male offspring, hence meaning lineage or ancestry
key_terms.لَيْسَ حَيْثُ تَذْهَبُ: It is not where you are going — an idiomatic correction meaning 'you have misunderstood the matter'

ai.seo_question: Does a curse from an Imam affect the believers among the cursed person's descendants?
ai.summary: Ali ibn Yaqteen, a trusted companion of Imam al-Kazim who served in the Abbasid court, expressed concern that Imam al-Sadiq's reported curse against his father Yaqteen (an Abbasid supporter) would affect him and his descendants. Imam al-Kazim reassured him with a vivid analogy: a believer born from a disbeliever's lineage is like a pebble embedded in a mud brick — when the rain (divine punishment) dissolves the brick (the disbeliever), the pebble (the believer) remains unharmed. This teaching establishes that divine punishment and blessing are strictly personal and not inherited through lineage.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Yaqteen, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I pitied from a supplication of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> against Yaqteen and what he begot’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Abu Al-Hassan! It is not where you are going with it. But rather, the Believer in the back of the disbeliever is at a status of the pebbles among the block. The rain comes and it washes the block, and it does not harm the pebbles anything’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ali ibn Yaqtin from abu al-Hassan Musa (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Once I said to the Imam, ‘I am afraid of the prayer of abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) against Yaqtin and his offspring.’

The Imam said, ‘O abu al-Hassan, it is not as you think. A believer in the back of an unbeliever is like a small piece of stone in a brick. Rain can wash away the brick but it never harms the solid piece of stone.’”
